paper_title: A Model-Independent Radio Telescope Dark Matter Search in the L and S Bands
notes: This is a model-independent radio telescope search for ultralight bosonic dark matter via radiative decay or annihilation to a quasimonochromatic radio line over 1020-2700 MHz. The reported limits are on the decay rate (lambda ~ 1e-32 s^-1) and the velocity-weighted annihilation cross section (<sigma v> ~ 1e-30 cm^3/s), NOT on a standard coupling constant like g_agamma. Although two-photon axion decay is mentioned as one possible channel, the primary results are presented as decay rate and cross-section limits vs frequency (mass), which do not map to any of the listed coupling enum types. Therefore coupling_type is null and no data points are extracted in the required coupling units. Local DM density assumed rho_NFW(rs)=0.471 GeV/cm^3 (Burkert: 0.487). 3-sigma exclusion (~99.7%, no exact 90/95% CL stated; defaulted to 0.90). Mass relates to frequency via m = 2*h*nu for decay assuming hv=m_chi c^2/2.
